name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
theme: the 12-month line · three trials, one question, two answers

meta.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with DLBCL-NOS, the most common aggressive lymphoma (~30% of NHL; median age at diagnosis in the 60s). Curable in the majority from the first line - and uniquely in oncology, the SECOND line was rewritten by three simultaneous randomized CAR-T trials that asked one question and returned two answers. EBV-positive DLBCL and T-cell/histiocyte-rich LBCL stay inside this spec (managed per the DLBCL-NOS pathway; THRLBCL routing pending registry confirmation). PMBCL and HGBL with MYC/BCL2 rearrangements are DIFFERENT pathway rows (DA-EPOCH-R family); transformed indolent lymphoma routes to the follicular row; CNS involvement exits to the CNS-lymphoma pathway.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where relapse TIMING is the biggest biomarker: primary-refractory or early-relapse (<=12 months) disease routes to second-line CAR-T on a randomized overall-survival win (ZUMA-7), late relapse keeps the salvage-to-transplant spine - and BELINDA sits on the same screen as the honest reminder that three randomized trials of one idea returned two answers. Frontline teaches the POLARIX discipline (a 5-year PFS win that has never become an OS win ranks as the tie it is), and the third-line menu renders the accelerated-approval ledger verbatim: o…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) / ICC (2022): DLBCL-NOS distinct from PMBCL, HGBL-MYC/BCL2, THRLBCL, EBV+ DLBCL, primary CNS lymphoma, leg-type
meta.response: Lugano 2014 criteria with the Deauville 5-point PET scale (end-of-treatment PET is the response instrument)

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis is in the 60s. Age routes real forks: the FLYER minimum was proven to 60, POLARIX enrolled to 80, and past 80 the honest standard is R-mini-CHOP - while PILOT proved age alone…
Patient.helpPatient: This lymphoma is most common after 60 - and there are proven plans at every age, including past 80.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: An NCCN-IPI factor and a real-world CAR-T lever: in the US consortium data, performance status - not age - predicted worse CAR-T outcomes.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited right now. Fitness, more than age, shapes which intensive options make sense.

Disease.label: Histology + MYC/BCL2 FISH (expert hematopathology)
Disease.help: The FISH result can rename the disease: MYC plus BCL2 rearrangements make high-grade B-cell lymphoma, a different row. PMBCL and transformation likewise exit before ranking.
Disease.helpPatient: A few lymphomas look like this one under the microscope but need different plans - a genetic test on the biopsy sorts them before anything else.

Disease.label: CNS involvement
Disease.help: Secondary CNS lymphoma needs high-dose-methotrexate-based, CNS-directed programs - none of the systemic cards below apply unmodified.
Disease.helpPatient: If the lymphoma has reached the brain or spinal fluid, the plan changes completely - that path has its own trainer row.

Disease.label: Stage group (Lugano)
Disease.help: Stage routes the menu: limited disease has randomized minimums; advanced disease is where the R-CHOP vs pola-R-CHP choice lives. Ranking waits for the scan.
Disease.helpPatient: Where the lymphoma is decides which of two very different plans applies - worth waiting for the full scan.

Disease.label: NCCN-IPI risk group
Disease.help: The forecast instrument, not a ranking lever: NCCN-IPI drives the relapse posterior, and the POLARIX card requires IPI>=2 because that is the label. The trial averages already contain the risk mix.
Disease.helpPatient: A five-factor score that says how hard this lymphoma tends to push back - it shapes follow-up intensity and one drug's eligibility, not the goal of cure.

Disease.label: Bulky disease (>=7.5 cm)
Disease.help: FLYER proved the 4-cycle minimum only in non-bulky (<7.5 cm) favorable disease - bulk closes that card, it does not just annotate it.
Disease.helpPatient: One large mass changes how little treatment is safe to try.

On treatment.label: End-of-treatment PET (Deauville)
On treatment.help: The response instrument (Lugano). The positive branch runs through a biopsy, not straight to salvage - and the posterior moves in both directions.
On treatment.helpPatient: The scan at the end of treatment. A clean scan means watchful follow-up without routine scans; a positive one means checking with a needle before changing plans.

Relapse routing.label: Relapse pattern (the 12-month line)
Relapse routing.help: The biggest biomarker this disease has, and it is a calendar: within 12 months routes to second-line CAR-T (randomized OS win); beyond it the transplant spine holds (CORAL: response 88% vs 46% across…
Relapse routing.helpPatient: WHEN the lymphoma came back matters as much as that it did - a quick return calls for the cell-therapy road.

Relapse routing.label: Transplant / intensive-therapy candidacy
Relapse routing.help: Transplant candidacy routes the relapse menu - and PILOT (median age 74) is the card that says intensive-therapy ineligibility does NOT mean cell-therapy ineligibility.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the strongest chemotherapy road is safe for you. If not, there is still a cell-therapy road built exactly for that situation.

Relapse routing.label: Prior CAR-T therapy
Relapse routing.help: Treatment history is a biomarker: after CAR-T failure the menu turns to CD20xCD3 bispecifics and ADCs - about a third of the pivotal bispecific populations were post-CAR-T.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the cell therapy has already been used decides which doors are still open - there are real options after it.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: 4x R-CHOP + 2 R (FLYER - the proven minimum, young favorable)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (limited stage, favorable) - confirm exact category via current version
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: one-third less chemotherapy than the historical six cycles; anthracycline cardiac exposure reduced in the population that keeps it longest
Newly diagnosed.patient: For limited, low-risk disease in younger fit patients: four cycles proved as good as six - less treatment, same cure.

Newly diagnosed.name: PET-directed R-CHOP (S1001 - scan decides cycle four's company)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (limited stage, PET-directed) - confirm exact category via current version
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 2 (practice-setting; established 4xR-CHOP-alone for PET-negative limited disease)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: four total cycles for most; radiotherapy and its field-shaped late effects only for the PET-positive minority
Newly diagnosed.patient: Start with three cycles; a scan then decides whether one more cycle finishes the job - nine in ten people avoid radiation entirely.
drugs: R-CHOP, PET-adapted (+/- involved-site RT for interim-PET-positive disease)

Newly diagnosed.name: R-CHOP x6 (the 25-year backbone)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (advanced stage) - confirm exact category via current version
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the known ledger: alopecia, neuropathy (vincristine), febrile neutropenia risk (G-CSF territory at 65+), anthracycline cardiac exposure
Newly diagnosed.patient: Six cycles of the combination that has cured most people with this disease for twenty years.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pola-R-CHP (POLARIX - the PFS win that ranks as the OS tie it is)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (advanced stage, IPI>=2) - confirm exact category via current version
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS primary met; OS no difference at 5 years
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: swaps vincristine's neuropathy for polatuzumab's (similar overall rates in-trial); febrile neutropenia comparable; same anthracycline
Newly diagnosed.patient: The newer combination keeps more people progression-free - and five years in, survival is the same as the classic program. The honest pitch is fewer relapses and fewer second-line treatments, not longer life.

Newly diagnosed.name: R-mini-CHOP (age >=80 - the honest full-intent dose)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (age >=80 / infirm) - confirm exact category via current version
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: attenuated but real: neutropenic risk dominates; geriatric assessment shapes every cycle
Newly diagnosed.patient: A gentler version of the curative program, built and proven specifically for people over 80 - the goal is still cure.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.evidence: historical series (teaching estimate, flagged); palliative-care integration randomized
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; progressive nodal and constitutional symptoms dominate
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice, and in this disease the contrast is stark - the card shows it plainly so the choice is truly informed.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Axi-cel, second line (ZUMA-7 - the randomized OS win)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (2L, refractory/early relapse) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - EFS and OS superiority
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS (grade >=3: 6%) and neurologic events (grade >=3: 21%) - a front-loaded toxicity ledger traded for a one-time treatment
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the lymphoma never left or came back within a year, one infusion of your own re-engineered immune cells beat the transplant road at keeping people alive.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Platinum salvage -> autologous transplant (late relapse - the spine holds)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (2L, late relapse, transplant-eligible) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: standard of care (CORAL-era randomized salvage data; teaching estimate flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the transplant block is intense but time-boxed; the pre-transplant PET is the go/no-go instrument
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A relapse after more than a year usually still answers to chemotherapy - stronger salvage to a clean scan, then the transplant, cures about half.
drugs: Platinum-based salvage (R-ICE / R-DHAP) -> BEAM-conditioned autologous transplant

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Liso-cel, 2L transplant-not-intended (PILOT - age is not the wall)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (2L, transplant-ineligible) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: notably gentle CAR-T profile in TRANSFORM/PILOT (grade 3 CRS ~1%); still a monitored treatment month
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Built for exactly the situation where the transplant road is closed: cell therapy proven in a 74-year-old-median population.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pola-BR (transplant-ineligible - the randomized ADC combination)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (R/R, transplant-ineligible) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized phase 2 (OS benefit over BR); full FDA approval
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias and polatuzumab neuropathy; bendamustine's T-cell toll matters if CAR-T is still on the table - sequence deliberately
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An antibody that delivers chemotherapy directly to the lymphoma cells, combined with two familiar drugs - proven to extend life in a randomized comparison.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Tafasitamab + lenalidomide (L-MIND - chemo-free, transplant-ineligible)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (R/R, transplant-ineligible) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias (lenalidomide), infusion reactions early; the gentlest sustained program on this screen
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A chemotherapy-free combination: an antibody plus a daily capsule, with responses that often last years in people who cannot have the intensive roads.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Glofitamab (fixed-duration bispecific - the CRL survivor)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+; post-CAR-T listed) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 pivotal (accelerated approval; confirmatory conversion unresolved)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS mostly in step-up (grade >=3: 4%) - manageable with the protocol; the fixed stop date is the quality-of-life argument
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An off-the-shelf antibody that recruits your T cells against the lymphoma - a fixed course with an end date, active even after cell therapy.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Epcoritamab (subcutaneous bispecific - conversion pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+; post-CAR-T listed) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 pivotal (accelerated approval; confirmatory PFS met / OS neutral)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS ~50% (grade 3: 2.5%), rare ICANS; subcutaneous delivery, continuous schedule
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An under-the-skin injection that recruits your T cells against the lymphoma - active after cell therapy, given until it stops working.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Loncastuximab tesirine (LOTIS-2 - the single-agent ADC)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas (3L+) - confirm exact category via current version
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 single-arm (accelerated approval; confirmatory PFS met, conversion filing pending)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: effusions/edema (the PBD payload's signature - dexamethasone premedication), photosensitivity, cytopenias
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A targeted antibody that carries its own chemotherapy into the lymphoma cell - one drug, every three weeks.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Selinexor (SADAL) - WITHDRAWN: the ledger's cautionary entry
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NOT on-label for DLBCL as of 2026-08 (withdrawn); myeloma indications unaffected
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: historical ledger: nausea, anorexia, fatigue, hyponatremia - the tolerability that helped keep the confirmatory question unanswered
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: This drug is no longer approved for this lymphoma - its maker gave up the approval rather than run the trial that would have tested it. The card stays visible because that story protects future patients.
drugs: Selinexor (XPO1 inhibitor) - withdrawn in this indication

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: historical pooled cohort (SCHOLAR-1) as context; palliative-care integration randomized
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort with symptoms managed well - a real chapter with real support, chosen with real numbers on the table.

JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

HBV SCREENING (the reactivation law): Hwang et al., 'Hepatitis B Virus Screening and Management for Patients With Cancer Prior to Therapy: ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion Update' (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3698-3715 - PMID 32716741, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): ALL patients anticipating systemic anticancer therapy tested with 3 tests (HBsAg, anti-HBc total Ig/IgG, anti-HBs) WITHOUT delaying therapy. Chronic HBV (HBsAg+): antiviral prophylaxis through and >=12 months after therapy. Past HBV (HBsAg-/anti-HBc+) + HIGH-RISK therapy (anti-CD20 antibodies, SCT): prophylaxis during and >=12 months after; monitoring only as an adherence-dependent alternative.
